sentences: `M = M + DATA` as binary32 on the LDS dword (RDNA2 ISA, `DS_ADD_F32`); the `_rtn_` form returns the old M.
No core SPIR-V atomic adds floats on Workgroup memory, so it is an `OpAtomicCompareExchange` loop with an `OpFAdd` (round to nearest even, `NoContraction`).
That is exact under contention: every update is one successful exchange of the value it read.
**Not measured:** how the LDS adder treats denormals and NaN payloads; the result is `OpFAdd`'s IEEE sum.
CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_lds_add_f32.py` (a value grid, the non-returning form, `offset:`, ties to even, -0 + +0, overflow to ±inf, seeded values, against a once-rounded double sum).
